note: An example hosts file for settings.py and bundle.sh: one file per host pair, kept outside the TensorFold tree (it names your hosts, their addresses and your paths). Every address here is a documentation address, every MAC a locally administered placeholder (02:...) and every GID the link-local address derived from that MAC: replace them all with the values read on your hosts. "fields" explains each field; settings.py ignores it and "note".

fields.pair: the pair's name: settings/<pair>/ in the bundle and the Copy directory's name
fields.label_prefix: put before every run's label ("r-" keeps a rehearsal's r-G1 .. apart from the gate's G1 ..); default none
fields.mtu: the RC path MTU both ends run at: 1024, 2048 or 4096, at most each port's active MTU; default 1024
fields.kind: the link kind both ends must report: cx5 (ConnectX, RoCE v2) or tb5 (Thunderbolt); default cx5
fields.window_mib: the window in MiB; on a Mac the window plus both ranks' staging fits the kext's 64 regions (at most 63 pieces of 4 MiB)
fields.rounds: the suite's rounds for G1 and G2; default 3
fields.port: the base UDP port of MCDMA's exchange: each run takes its own, port + 10 per run; default 7610
fields.name: the link name both ends give MCDMA; default gate1594
fields.connect_timeout_s: how long a run waits for the other end to connect, s; default 120 (G5's runs take 30)
fields.hosts: exactly two hosts by name, the Mac first (host a) and the Linux host second (host b)
fields.os: macos or linux: which run script and prep lines
fields.script: the run script in the bundle; default by os
fields.library: libmcdma-fabric on that host: an absolute path, or $BUNDLE/... for the one build_mcdma.sh puts next to the scripts
fields.gid: the GID index: 0 on a Mac (the MCDMA kext has only index 0), the RoCE v2 index on Linux (often 1: /sys/class/infiniband/<device>/ports/1/gid_attrs/types/)
fields.via: the meeting interface, a slash, then the OTHER host's address on the same layer-2 segment (MCDMA admits only that peer)
fields.netdev: the ConnectX port's network interface; on a Mac with "ports", it picks the cabled port
fields.ports: a Mac with two ConnectX ports: per netdev, its device (rdma_<netdev>), mac and gid_addr
fields.device: the RDMA device (ibv_devices on Linux, rdma_mcrdmaN on a Mac)
fields.mac: the ConnectX port's MAC, for the other host's static neighbour
fields.gid_addr: the address of the port's GID (the IPv6 link-local one), for the other host's static neighbour
fields.expected_kext_uuid: a Mac: kextstat's UUID for org.mcdma.cx5.native; the pre-flight WARNs on any other and compare.py fails the gate on that WARN
fields.restore_rdma: a Mac, required: MCDMA's tools/restore-rdma.py on that Mac, for the prep line
fields.native_check: a Mac, required: MCDMA's cx5-native-check on that Mac, for the prep line's GID check
fields.ssh: how host a reaches host b: an alias from ~/.ssh/config (such as "linux-b"); default the host's name
fields.ssh_opts: extra ssh and scp options; default none (put keys and users in ~/.ssh/config)
fields.active_mtu: host b's active MTU as ibv_devinfo reads it: at 4096 PLAN says N/A for G5a
fields.free: true only for a box a link drop may take down: only then is G4 planned
fields.caution: a line PLAN prints at its top for that host

name: gate1594

gb10.caution: shared with other jobs: no G4 (it is not free), and run G1 and G2 while its ConnectX port is idle (its port also carries 198.51.100.21)
